summary: Type-safe, object-oriented platform powering enterprise backends, Android runtimes, and large distributed data pipelines.

rows.means: top-level class visible to all packages in the project
rows.consequence: In Java, every public class must reside in a file matching its exact name (Name.java). Encapsulates state and methods.

rows.means: the entry point the runtime looks for
rows.consequence: public so the runtime may call it, static so it runs without an instance of the class existing, and returning nothing because the exit status is set separately.

rows.means: prints formatted text followed by a newline to stdout
rows.consequence: Buffered stream output to the operating system terminal; automatically invokes the object's toString() method.

rows.means: allocates an object on the managed heap and runs its constructor
rows.consequence: Objects live on the collected heap; the references to them live on the stack of the thread using them, which is the distinction that makes the collector possible.

rows.means: inherits from a single superclass / implements multiple interfaces
rows.consequence: Java allows single class inheritance to prevent the diamond problem, but permits implementing any number of interface contracts.

rows.means: pure contract of methods / partial implementation with state
rows.consequence: Interfaces define behavior contracts (can also have default methods); abstract classes can hold instance state and constructors.

rows.code:
final (variable / method / class)
public final class java.lang.String
rows.means: constant value / cannot be overridden / cannot be subclassed
rows.consequence: A final class cannot be subclassed, which is what lets the standard string type promise that an instance never changes after it is made — and that promise is what makes sharing one between threads safe.

rows.means: compact syntax for immutable data-carrier classes (Java 14+)
rows.consequence: Automatically generates constructor, getters, equals(), hashCode(), and toString() for clean immutable data objects.

rows.means: automatically closes AutoCloseable resources on block exit
rows.consequence: Guarantees database connections, files, and sockets close even if exceptions occur, eliminating manual finally cleanup.

rows.code: throws Exception vs throw new Exception()
rows.means: declares checked exception in method signature / throws exception
rows.consequence: Checked exceptions must either be handled with a try/catch block or declared in the throws signature, verified by the compiler.

rows.means: dynamically resizing array backed by standard interface
rows.consequence: Program to the interface (List), not the implementation (ArrayList), allowing you to swap in LinkedList without breaking callers.

rows.means: hash table providing O(1) average lookup by key
rows.consequence: Relies on equals() and hashCode() contracts on the key class; if hashCode() is poorly implemented, lookups degrade to O(n).

rows.means: functional processing pipeline over collections
rows.consequence: Executes lazily: intermediate operations (.filter, .map) only compute when a terminal operation (.collect, .count) is triggered.

rows.means: container object that may or may not contain a non-null value
rows.consequence: Designed to eliminate NullPointerExceptions by forcing the caller to explicitly handle the empty case.

rows.code: enum Direction { NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST }
rows.means: type-safe enumeration with methods and fields
rows.consequence: Java enums are full-featured classes that can implement interfaces, hold fields, and define specific constructor behaviors.

rows.means: tells compiler this method must override a superclass method
rows.consequence: Catches bugs at compile time if the method signature does not exactly match the parent class or interface method.

rows.means: references parent superclass / references current object instance
rows.consequence: super() invokes the parent constructor; this.field disambiguates between instance fields and parameter names.

rows.means: acquires an intrinsic monitor lock for thread synchronization
rows.consequence: Guarantees that only one thread executes the protected block at a time, preventing race conditions on shared state.

rows.means: ensures reads and writes are visible immediately across all CPU threads
rows.consequence: Prevents the compiler and the processor from keeping the variable in a register or a cache, so a write by one thread is visible to the next thread that reads it.

rows.means: compiler infers the static type from the right-hand initializer
rows.consequence: Available in Java 10+ for local variables. Keeps code concise without sacrificing static compile-time type safety.

rows.means: compact implementation of an interface with a single abstract method
rows.consequence: Passed directly wherever such an interface is expected, which is what lets a method take behaviour as an argument without a named class existing for it.

rows.code:
<T extends Comparable<T>>
// erased to Object in the bytecode
rows.means: compile-time type parameters with bounded constraints
rows.consequence: Implemented by erasure: the compiler checks the types and then removes them, so the runtime sees the unparameterised type. That is why you cannot ask, at run time, what a collection was parameterised with.
